citation.title: Rank Reduction AutoEncoders for Mechanical Design: Advancing Novel and Efficient Data-Driven Topology Optimization
citation.authors: Ismael Ben-Yelun, Mohammed El Fallaki Idrissi, Jad Mounayer, Sebastian Rodriguez, Francisco Chinesta
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (30 Jan 2026; only version on the abs page), full text read from https://arxiv.org/html/2601.23269

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (excluded). Headline: RRAE-plus-MLP surrogates give accurate, efficient forward stress prediction and inverse geometry recovery on a SIMP half-MBB dataset; accuracy is measured only against SIMP/FE ground truth, with no runtime comparison.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not coded (excluded at full text); no runtimes are reported anywhere in the article.

notes: Excluded under PROTOCOL §4 (no comparison with a classical method). The article reports no speed, cost or design-quality comparison with any classical optimizer. Its efficiency statements (abstract; Sec. 5.1.1; Sec. 6) are qualitative, have no timing, hardware or training-cost data, and concern replacing forward FE analysis. Inverse outputs are compared only with the SIMP ground truth: L2 reconstruction loss 20.59%/20.22% (scalar QoI), 6.38%/7.63% (1D field) and 5.74%/7.80% (2D field), train/test (Sec. 5.1.2, 5.2.2, 5.3.2), plus one FE re-analysis example (Fig. 10). Dataset: 100 SIMP designs of an 80×80 half-MBB beam from the top88.m OC code with volume fraction swept from 0.1 to 0.9, plus 20 test designs (Sec. 5). Judgment call for the verifier: if the abstract's qualitative speed wording is read as a speed claim against TO, the record would enter the speed stratum with a qualitative primary outcome; R3 would then fail (no training or data cost) and R4 would likely fail (image-type reconstruction metric, apart from one FE check). No code or data availability statement found. Screening code was I-UNCLEAR.
